name: Acromegaly

category.name: General Systemic

what_to_bring: Sleep Study that meets current AASM or CMS Guidelines for a Type I or Type II sleep study (Type III or Type IV NOT allowed) performed no more than 12 months before the AME exam. (If currently treated for OSA, see that page.)
A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with a cardiologist no more than 90 days before the AME exam.
Labs to include lipids and hemoglobin A1c performed no more than 90 days before the AME exam.
Echocardiogram (Echo) . Copies of a 2- D and Doppler flow study report performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam.
24-hour cardiac monitor performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam.

A Neuropsychological evaluation that meets **FAA Specifications for Neuropsychological Evaluations for Potential Neurocognitive Impairment** from a clinic visit with the treating neuropsychologist no more than 90 days before the AME exam.
Other records and testing: Copies of prior records and any testing already performed by the treating physician.
All items listed on the correct row of the PITUITARY ADENOMA page.

It must include a detailed summary of the history of the condition; current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any); physical exam findings; results of any testing performed; diagnosis; assessment; plan (prognosis); and follow-up.

rows.evaluation_data_html:
Submit the following for FAA review:

  • 1. Sleep Study that meets current AASM or CMS Guidelines for a Type I or Type II sleep study (Type III or Type IV NOT allowed) performed no more than 12 months before the AME exam. (If currently treated for OSA, see that page.)
  • 2. A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with a cardiologist no more than 90 days before the AME exam.

It should include a summary of the history of the condition or diagnosis; current medications, dosages, and side effects (if any); clinical exam findings; results of any testing performed; diagnosis; assessment and plan (prognosis); and follow-up.

  • 3. Labs to include lipids and hemoglobin A1c performed no more than 90 days before the AME exam.
  • 4. Echocardiogram (Echo). Copies of a 2- D and Doppler flow study report performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam.
  • 5. 24-hour cardiac monitor performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam.

≥ 24-hour cardiac monitor (such as a Holter, Zio Patch, etc.). It should have atrial and ventricular ectopic counts; hourly tabular data to include the longest pause duration and counts of all pauses > 2.0 or 2.5 seconds; heart rate (max, min, and average); other histograms and frequency graphs; and percentage of atrial fibrillation/flutter.

  • 6. A Neuropsychological evaluation that meets **FAA Specifications for Neuropsychological Evaluations for Potential Neurocognitive Impairment** from a clinic visit with the treating neuropsychologist no more than 90 days before the AME exam.
  • 7. Other records and testing: Copies of prior records and any testing already performed by the treating physician.
  • 8. All items listed on the correct row of the PITUITARY ADENOMA page.
